title: Over What Period a Corporate Travel Programmes Billing Is Read for an Air Ticket Fare Brands Charge
content:
Where a Corporate Travel Programmes programme stands against an Air Ticket Fare Brands booking, its billing is read over a longer period once the programme's current contract term has settled, and how much longer depends on how often the programme is invoiced.

## 1. The window

1.1 Where the programme is invoiced annually and its current contract term has run 6 months or more, the programme's billing is read over the whole of the current contract term.

1.2 Where the programme is invoiced monthly or quarterly and its current contract term has run 6 months or more, it is read over the last 12 months.

1.3 In every other case no such re-reading of the window is made.

## 2. The two readings

The invoicing frequency is a term of the Corporate Travel Programmes programme standing against the booking. The contract term is counted in months from the programme's contract start date to today, and both of the first two rows require it to have run 6 months or more.

A programme whose contract has run fewer than 6 months falls outside both rows however it is invoiced.

## 3. Condition matrix

| Invoicing frequency | Months the current contract term has run | The billing is read over |
| --- | --- | --- |
| annual | 6 or more | the whole of the current contract term |
| monthly or quarterly | 6 or more | the last 12 months |
| any | fewer than 6 | no such re-reading |

## 4. Worked readings, on hypothetical figures

A programme invoiced annually whose contract began 19 months ago: the term has run 6 months or more, so its billing is read over the whole 19 months of the current contract term.

A programme invoiced quarterly whose contract began 19 months ago: its billing is read over the last 12 months, and the 7 months of the contract term before that fall outside the window.

A programme invoiced annually whose contract began 4 months ago: 4 months is fewer than 6, and no such re-reading is made.
